newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down, Central Bank intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down, Central Bank intervenes.

text.p: The Philippine peso surrendered gains on Friday to end at 26.290 against the dollar from the previous day's 26.286 after the Central Bank heavily bought dollars throughout the session, traders said.
Traders said the Central Bank bought some $80 to 88 million at 26.278 to 26.288 pesos to limit the peso's rise, after a flood of incoming dollars from foreign investors.
The peso average rose to 26.285 from 26.288.
The peso had nudged up to a day-high of 26.278 pesos after opening at a day-low of 26.298. Volume swelled to $246.20 million from $106 million.

"Banks were expecting a weaker peso because of the usual interest arbitrage play for the weekend. But it did the opposite," a trader said, pointing out that most of the day's trades were done at a strong peso rate.
Dealers said foreign investors came in due to the increasing confidence in President Fidel Ramos' ability to further strengthen the economy.
